deadline.value: President's PhD Scholarship (college-wide, open to all nationalities) rounds: apply by Nov 2, 2026, Jan 11, 2027 or Mar 1, 2027 (23:59 UK time). Physics accepts PhD applications all year; the Theory group lists a Feb 1 deadline 'each year' (shown with the 2026 date).
deadline.quote: Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 2 November 2026 and are awarded a scholarship will be notified by 31 January 2027. | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 11 January 2027 | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 1 March 2027

also.quote: PhD applications can be made all year-round, but we encourage all applicants interested in scholarships to apply as early as possible, since most scholarships have early deadlines driven by the funding requirements.
Our application deadline is *** 1 February 2026*** each year.

supervisor.value: Not needed before applying: the Theory group says you need not contact a supervisor, and the Matter community considers you for all available projects. Naming a preferred supervisor helps route your application (Light community). Exception: President's PhD Scholarship applicants must already have a supervisor who has agreed to supervise them.
supervisor.quote: Also, it is not necessary for you to contact a prospective supervisor directly, you can simply indicate potential names of supervisors you may interested in working with.

also.quote: You can highlight your preference for a specific project in your application. However, we will consider you for all available projects.
PROPOSED SUPERVISOR: Naming a prospective supervisor is the most helpful information that you could provide to ensure that your application will be correctly allocated.
You must have made contact with a supervisor in an academic department at Imperial College London who has agreed to supervise your research project.

funding.value: A limited number of fully funded studentships (fees and living costs). Studentships for overseas applicants are very restricted: most overseas students bring home-country scholarships or self-fund (Matter community page). President's PhD Scholarships are open to all nationalities but very competitive.
funding.quote: We typically have a limited number of fully-funded PhD studentships that pay both your fees and your living expenses. | Studentships for overseas applicants are very restricted. We typically take a few overseas students who have scholarships from their home country, or in some cases are self-funded.

also.quote: This competitive scheme has higher than usual eligibility requirements, attracting candidates that show excellent academic performance and promising research potential.

entry_route.value: A First-class or at least 2:1 honours degree (or equivalent), typically in Physics, with a Direct PhD option. The Theory group says an MSc is a significant advantage but not a prerequisite.
entry_route.quote: Applicants should have, or be expecting, a First Class honours degree, or at least an Upper Second Class honours (2:1) or equivalent degree.

also.quote: It is also a significant advantage to have done an MSc course in theoretical physics or the Cambridge Part III but this is not a pre-requisite.

app_fee.value: No application fee for doctoral degrees such as the PhD (master's applications cost GBP 90)
app_fee.quote: You do not need to pay an application fee for: | Postgraduate Doctoral degrees (e.g. PhD, EngD) | £90 for all Master's applications (MSc, MPH, MRes)

fee_waiver.value: PhD applications carry no application fee, so no waiver is needed

english_waiver.value: Exempt only with a UK-degree-equivalent qualification from a listed country (Australia, Canada, Guyana, Ireland, Malta, New Zealand, South Africa, UK, USA, West Indies); India is not listed

notes: There is no single Physics PhD course page; details come from the research-community pages (Light, Matter, Theory), and several still show 2026-cycle dates. Imperial's English levels are TOEFL 92 (Standard) or 100 (Higher), or 4.5/5.0 on the new scale.
